cases.name: Theresa Romano
cases.about: Patricia Hinger, one of Romano’s two daughters, said she was thankful law enforcement didn’t forget about her mom. Hinger only had a few memories of her mother and relied on her family to fill in the gaps, but one moment was unforgettable—learning to figure skate on the ice with her mom. “When I was about two years old, she put me on ice skates down at Pickwick Ice rink in California,” Hinger said. “I started taking lessons when I was about seven years old after she had passed.” Skating at the Pickwick Ice rink at the age of seven Hinger was surprised the people there still remembered her mom. “I took up figure skating in her memory,” she said. “It was something that I could do to be close to her since she wasn’t here anymore.”

cases.name: Janell Ruth Bowen Wright
cases.narrative:
On 11/21/2023, her body was found on fire in a barrel in Henderson, NV by the Henderson Fire Department after they responded to a report of a bin on fire in the 1700 block of Sunset Rd in Nenderson, NV.

He allegedly strangled her and hid her in a metal drum for days before setting her body on fire.

A witness told police on 11/18/2023, she saw Wright on top of Bowen appearing to strangle her while she was lying face down on the ground, according to the report. At one point she reported hearing him say, “Die b—-,” the report said. When they looked into the window one last time, she said she knew Bowen was dead, the report said.

During an autopsy, the Clark County Coroner’s officer discovered “significant evidence of asphyxiation by strangulation,” marks on her upper back, three fractured ribs, and “apparent evidence of vaginal trauma,” the report said.

cases.name: Susan Lillian Morgan
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "On the morning of Independence Day, July 4th, 2023, we lost a beacon of light and transformation, Susan Morgan. Her sudden departure has left an unfillable void in countless lives she has touched, directly and indirectly, through her life's work.

Born in Longmeadow, Massachusetts to Paul James Meals and Estelle Boisvert Meals, Susan was an emblem of adventurous spirit and an inexhaustible zest for life from her youth. Not only a spiritually awakened soul, Susan had an insatiable love for reading, poetry, and was a lifelong artist who painted with colors as vivid and resonant as her own spirit

In her 20s, alongside her husband John Heinemann, she co-founded Hi-Tech Boats, building high-performance racing sailboats that dominated seas globally. This venture was an embodiment of Susan's innovative spirit and her knack for turning dreams into reality.

However, it was in her second act where Susan truly found her calling. As the founder of Mystic Dream Center, Susan emerged as an Author, Teacher, Soul Worker, and Speaker. Her mission was simple yet profound: to empower individuals to navigate life in higher vibrations, to follow their passions, and to comprehend the messages carried in their dreams.

Returning to Mystic, Connecticut, in 1999, she opened a Bed & Breakfast and initiated her dream circles alongside Robert Moss. The powerful insight and healing that these circles bestowed on participants led Susan to devote her life to expanding consciousness, sowing the seeds for Mystic Dream Center.

With her compassionate nature and profound knowledge, she turned Mystic Dream Center into a live weekly TV show in 2006. As the host, she invited guests, taught classes, and answered viewers' questions about dreams. Her exceptional skills and vibrant personality shone through, making it the highest-rated show on public access television.

Susan's life took another turn when she moved to East Hampstead, New Hampshire in 2008, marking a decade of dedication to hosting dream circles across New England and beyond. Her journey then led her to Henderson, Nevada in 2018 to be closer to her beloved grandchildren and father.

In Henderson, Susan's vision took physical form in Mystic Dream, a Metaphysical shop. She offered classes, meditation supplies, and neurofeedback services for those struggling with mental and physical conditions. Her healing touch was palpable. Her clients often left sessions moved to tears, claiming she had saved their lives.

To thousands, Susan was an exceptional woman: an empowering guide, a mentor, a unique teacher, a fearless warrior for truth and justice. She had a passion for igniting the spark in others, often sacrificing her own time to help those feeling lost or troubled. Susan was a mother figure to many in her life, who fiercely loved her children and grandchildren. Nothing made her happier than spending time adventuring and doting on her family.

Susan spent her whole life connecting with the Spirit Realm and her Spirit Helpers, working as a gifted Psychic Medium, authoring many books on Death, Consciousness, and Dreams. Her energy and dedication continue to reverberate in Mystic Dream's larger community, a testament to her unwavering belief in spiritual growth and personal transformation. Her teachings, workshops, and retreats have paved the way for seekers on their spiritual journey, helping them uncover hidden truths and awaken their inner power.

As we mourn her passing, we also celebrate Susan Morgan's extraordinary life. She leaves behind a legacy of love and enlightenment in her children - Gabriel, Charlotte, and James, their families, and the countless lives she touched. Susan's light will continue to guide us through the path she carved with love, dedication, and an undying belief in the power of dreams. In her absence, her family is comforted by Susan's strong beliefs that she was to return to a higher realm back to the Stars from which she came and will continue to be accessible to us, in our Dreams."
